title: A JSONDecodeError indicates that the JSON syntax could not be parsed.
body: A JSONDecodeError is an error that occurs when `json.loads()` or `json.load()` cannot parse the JSON syntax. First, check the placement of commas, quotation marks, and curly braces.
detail: JSON looks similar to a Python dictionary, but its syntax is stricter. String keys must be enclosed in double quotes, and commas are required between items. The line, column, and character information in error messages provides clues to pinpoint the location of the problem.

title: utf-8-sig is useful when reading UTF-8 files that contain a BOM
body: A UTF-8 BOM may appear as U+FEFF at the start of decoded text. In JSON it can cause a BOM-related JSONDecodeError; in CSV it may attach to the first header.
detail: Use utf-8-sig when the source bytes are UTF-8 with a BOM rather than as a generic fix for every decoding error.

title: "ensure_ascii=False" is often used to save Korean characters as-is.
body: If you use `ensure_ascii=False` with `json.dumps()`, Korean characters are saved as human-readable text rather than being converted to the `\uXXXX` format. This is useful when checking Korean configuration files or logs.
detail: By default, non-ASCII characters may be stored in Unicode escape format. While the data itself is not incorrect, it makes it difficult for humans to open and review the file. When saving flashcards or Korean description data, it is recommended to use both `ensure_ascii=False` and `encoding='utf-8'`.

title: Ensure that JSON is stored in a readable format and verified for safety
body: When saving JSON, the combination of `ensure_ascii=False`, `indent=2`, and `encoding='utf-8'` is often used. When reading JSON, you should check for both `JSONDecodeError` and encoding issues.
detail: `indent=2` makes the structure easier for humans to read, `ensure_ascii=False` displays Korean characters as-is, and `encoding='utf-8'` specifies the file encoding. Conversely, if garbled text or parsing errors occur during reading, the system checks the JSON syntax, file encoding, and the presence of a BOM in that order.
